To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
older and younger adults have different preferences in terms of the size and style of print for medication labels.
older adults have slower reading speeds and higher error rates than younger adults, and that these differences can be minimized by the use of certain print characteristics.
older adults read more slowly and make more errors on medication labels than do younger adults, and that font size is more important for readability than is font weight or style for older adults.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of font type, size, weight, and color, as well as the effects of the type of label (bottle versus flat) on older and younger adult reading speed and error rate.
the development of a model of the effects of age and task complexity on the use of information in decision-making by older adults.
the development of an effective method of presenting information in a manner that is easily read by older people.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is not a one size fits all approach to medication labels.
the use of a larger font, boldface, and sans serif typeface on medication labels would be beneficial to the older adult.
there are no significant differences in reading speeds, error rates, or subjective evaluations for the different print types.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
older adults are slower and more error-prone than younger adults when reading medication label print.
the readability of medication label information is affected by the font size and weight of the print.
there is no one best font, size, or weight of print for older and younger adult medication label users.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the font type, size, and weight used on a prescription drug label can have a significant impact on the reading time and error rate of both older and younger adults.
older adults can benefit from larger font size and bold print on medication labels.
the design of medication label print should be based on the age group for which the labels are designed.
